entries.title: The calculator build has been failing since the Pi game landed
entries.body: `app_pi.c` calls `nt_append` without including `ui/numtext.h`. The host preview took it as a warning and drew a perfect screenshot; the fxSDK build runs `-Werror=implicit-function-declaration` and stopped, so there has been no `.g3a` since 1.1.0 and the tagged release for 1.2.2 could not exist. The include is one line; the reason it went unseen for four merges is that the two builds disagreed about which warnings matter, so the preview now compiles with the same `-Werror=implicit-function-declaration` as the calculator and the candidate `.g3a` cannot be the only thing that finds it.

entries.title: The committed WebAssembly build is rebuilt from these sources
entries.body: , so the simulator on the site is the same code as the screenshots again. Its smoke runs (`down,exe` and the worker path) pass. **Unverified on device.**

entries.title: The screen checker can see a label sitting on a border
entries.body: it compared rectangles, so two things that merely touched were "not overlapping" and passed. The menu's first-run hint spent eleven merged pull requests with its ascenders on the bottom tile border, and 97 green screenshots said nothing about it. `scr_frame` is traced now - `scr_fill` records only panels of 8x4 or more, and a two-pixel border is exactly the size that goes wrong - and a label within two pixels of any frame, inside or out, fails the run. Checked against the old layout: it reports the hint and nothing else, so the rule has teeth without inventing work on the other 96 screens. `docs/design.md` lists it. **Unverified on device.**

entries.title: The site was not deploying at all
entries.body: `node scripts/gen-tools.mjs` has failed on every push since the four V2 tools landed, because each says in its own words what it does and `site/src/toolCopy.js` still listed twenty-two of them. The build reported "registry tool \"factor\" (Prime factors) has no copy" and stopped, so the last successful deployment predates Prime factors, Percentages, the Formula book and the Pi game. All four are in `toolCopy.js` now, with their real screenshots, and are in the "own words" set that needs proofreading.

entries.title: The download picks the newest build by version, not by file date
entries.body: `dist/` is a git checkout, so every `.g3a` in it is written at the same moment and the order the filesystem hands back decided which one the page offered. It offered 1.0.0 while 1.1.0 sat beside it. The fallback compares the numbers in the file name now, and a build's commit and date are dropped when the bytes came from a different file than the one `BUILD.txt` describes.

entries.title: CodeRabbit, configured in the repository instead of a dashboard
entries.body: `.coderabbit.yaml` tells the reviewer what this project actually breaks on - `src/core` must not include gint or libm, a screen may only use the nine palette colours with 2 px ink borders and a 3 px shadow under the selected item, a new core function needs a test with a concrete vector, a regenerated table is not a code change, and files are written to flash only at session end. Generated files, images, binaries and the site lockfile are out of scope, poems and UML diagrams are off, and automatic approvals are off because merging here depends on whether anyone ran the build on a calculator. `tools/check_coderabbit.py` parses the YAML with its own small reader - no new dependency - and rejects an unknown key, a `path_instructions` glob that matches no file (how a rule for a renamed directory stops applying), a tool switched on with no config file or for a language the repository does not contain, tabs and CRLF. `make coderabbit-check` runs it and CI runs that. Installing the GitHub App is the one step a commit cannot do; `docs/CODERABBIT.md` has the four clicks. **Unverified on device.**

entries.title: A version number that moves with the work, and a check that it did
entries.body: the tree said 1.1.0 through fourteen merged pull requests, so the About screen, the `.g3a` name and the website would have disagreed with the changelog the moment anything shipped. The rule is now that every change bumps the version in the same commit - patch for a fix or a doc, minor for a feature, major only for a storage-layout change - and the version of record is 1.2.0. `tools/ bump_version.py` rewrites `version.txt`, the `src/version.h` fallback and the example file name in `CMakeLists.txt` in one command (`make bump-minor`, `make bump-patch`), and `--check` compares those against the changelog heading and the README badge, naming each file that disagrees. `make test` runs it, and so does CI, so a forgotten bump fails a build instead of shipping. 21 Python tests cover the arithmetic and the rewriting, including that a bad version is refused before any file is touched. The README's version badge now links to the releases page rather than to `releases/tag/v<version>`, because between a bump and a release there is no such tag and a badge pointing at a 404 is a lie about a page. **Unverified on device.**

entries.title: Percentages tool
entries.body: the four questions a paper asks - percentage change, add or take a percentage, reverse percentage, compound growth or depreciation - on one Math screen, with the working written out under the answer. The point of the reverse question is that it divides (`34 / (1 - 15/100) = 40`), which is what people get wrong by adding 15% of 34 back on. `src/core/percent.c` with 41 checks covers the vectors (500 at 4.5% for 7 years is 680.43; a car at 12% for 5 years keeps 52.8%), zero years, a negative rate, and the three questions with no answer - a change from zero, a 100% discount, a period count outside 0..200 - each of which is a sentence on screen rather than a 0 or an inf. One bug caught by the tests before the screen existed: the fast exponentiation gave up on an overflow by returning the *principal*, so a question with an unshowable answer said "no growth". **Unverified on device.**

entries.title: The formula book
entries.body: the IB AA HL, Physics 2025 and Chemistry 2025 booklet content, as a Study tile called Formula book. The booklets are plain text in `Bench/formulas/`, one `.txt` per booklet, so a teacher (or you) can add one without a rebuild - the list shows every file in the folder and its first `#` line as the description. The viewer scrolls a line at a time and jumps a **topic** at a time with LEFT/RIGHT, headings coloured red, blue and ink by level. New `src/core/formula.c` holds the line and heading arithmetic with 40 checks, including that a jump ignores `###` sub-headings - with those counted, a booklet with a heading every few lines moved five lines a press, which is not a section. **The content is a transcription nobody has proofread yet**: the PDFs print formulae as images, so the text was typed, and it is marked as unproofread in three places - the first line of every booklet, `docs/samples/formulas/ needs-human-proofreading/README.md`, and the help page. Treat an unproofed line as unchecked.

entries.title: The Pi game
entries.body: a Study tile. The digits you have earned stay on screen, grouped five to a line; type the next ones, EXE checks them, and the first wrong digit costs a life. Three lives, F2 gives the next digit away and costs one - a hint that is free is not part of a game - and the round ends with how far you got and the best of the session. Nothing is written to the card, so the best score lives and dies with the session, which is what the file-write rule allows. The digits are `src/core/pi.c`: 200 of them, and `tests/test_pi.c` checks the table against a Rabinowitz-Wagon spigot computed from the algorithm rather than copied - a typo in the table cannot hide by being duplicated in the test (40 checks, first 100 digits plus the human check that the 100th decimal is 9). `pi_match` stops at the first wrong digit so a guess that runs off the end cannot read past the table. **Unverified on device.**

entries.title: Prime factors, on its own screen in Math
entries.body: factorisation existed, three levels down a list of nine Number theory functions, which is not where anyone looks for it. The new screen takes a number up to 18 digits and shows the factorisation written out - `360 = 2^3 x 3^2 x 5` - with the four numbers that follow from it: divisor count, divisor sum, totient and square-free part, plus how many distinct primes and whether the number is a perfect square. F2 halves the number and factors again, which is the question that usually comes next. New in `core/numtheory.c`, each with vectors checked by hand (1091 checks in that suite): `nt_factor_text` (exact buffer arithmetic, so a text of exactly the buffer's length is accepted and one byte less refused), `nt_divisor_count`, `nt_divisor_sum` (the geometric series without a division, wrapping checked), `nt_factor_radical` and `nt_factor_is_square`. **Unverified on device**: how long the rho routine takes on a real CPU for a hard 18-digit semiprime, and the screen draws no progress bar because of it.

entries.title: About says who made it
entries.body: the page was one screenful of version numbers. It now says whose work it is (Sarang, `github.com/sarang-cmd`), what it is, how it was made - maths in plain C tested without a calculator, screens a thin layer over gint, every doc picture a real simulator frame, builds from GitHub Actions - and keeps the build facts and the Exam Mode promise at the end. The page is longer than the screen, so it scrolls with the bar and `UP/DOWN`; scrolling reuses `core/help.c`'s tested rules. Tour 84 and 85 are its two ends. Also: `src/version.h`'s fallback said 1.0.0 while `version.txt` said 1.1.0, so the simulator's About screen was a release behind the add-in it was drawing - the fallback is 1.1.0 now. **Unverified on device.**

entries.title: Three more settings, and three places they reach
entries.body: Settings had five rows and two of them were read-only information. It has eight now, and each one does something: * **Opens on** - which category the home screen starts on, so someone who lives in Science does not press F3 every launch. * **Show hint line** - the first-run line on the home screen can be turned off for good without having to open Help first. * **Pacer clock red at** - minutes remaining when the Pacer's "Left mm:ss" line turns red, 0 to never. Default 5.

entries.title: The Tools category, centred
entries.body: "so awkward" was about Tools holding two tiles hard against the left margin with a third of the screen empty beside them. A row that is not full is centred under the one above it now, which leaves a full row exactly where it was. `src/core/layout.c` (21 native checks: full and short rows, a row wider than the screen, an empty row, the per-row count at a page boundary). Study's fourth tile and Science's short row move with it, since they were the same shape of problem. **Unverified on device.**

entries.title: The page indicator, and the missing Math title bar
entries.body: a category with more than six tools paged with two 4 px squares and a hole punched in the current one - "too subtle" was the report, and it was right: at 384 px that reads as dust. The indicator is now a bordered pill reading `1 / 2` with an arrow on each side that leads somewhere (only the live ones are drawn; a greyed one would be shade on paper at 1.3:1, which the screen checker rejects). The pill takes the space it needs only in categories that page, so every other category keeps the full grid. Chasing it found a second bug: the centring maths counted every tool in the category rather than the tools on the page, so Math's nine tools meant three rows of height, a negative offset, and the first row drawn over the title bar - the Math category had no title at all since the V2 push. Both are fixed, and `tests/test_pageind.c` checks the label, the arrow states and the clamping (31 checks), including the 10 / 12 two-digit case and a buffer one byte too small. **Unverified on device.**

entries.title: A scrollbar on every screen that scrolls
entries.body: a Notes file, a deck list, the study log, the root finder's iteration table and a help page all scrolled with nothing on screen saying so. The bar is now three pixels wide (it was two, a hairline at 384 px), ink thumb on a shade track, 12:1 and 4:1 in the palette with no new colours. It is drawn only when there is something off-screen, and the position is a fraction of the list, so the last screen shows the thumb at the bottom and nothing is drawn for a list that fits. **Unverified on device**: the bar is checked in the simulator against the pixel rules (`make check-screens`), not on the calculator's panel.

entries.title: A folder full of notes that the add-in could not see
entries.body: three matching bugs, all on the way *out* of the filesystem rather than in it. The glob was built as `*` plus the extension, which CASIOWIN's `BFile_FindFirst` answers with nothing on some OS versions; the extension test was case sensitive, so a Windows copy saved as `.MD` was invisible; and the OS's `.`/`..` entries were not filtered. The rules are now `src/core/filelist.c` (56 native checks: case, leading dots, separators, double extensions, a buffer one byte too small), the listing tries both wildcard spellings and filters in C, and the empty screen names the folder and says the case does not matter. **Unverified on device**: the two-glob retry exists because of how CASIOWIN is documented, and only a calculator can confirm which spelling its Fugue build wants.

entries.title: EXIT goes back where you came from
entries.body: closing a tool used to land on the home screen with Study selected, first tile, every single time - so a Maths or Science session meant walking back to the right category after every tool. The add-in now keeps a small stack of the screens it came through (`src/core/nav.c`, 525 native checks over push/pop, repeat pushes, a full stack and 500 random presses). EXIT and the help screen's way out both walk back one screen at a time, and the home screen remembers the category and the tile you were on instead of resetting itself. Two tour scripts record it: `78_back_to_maths` and `79_back_from_settings_about`.

entries.title: The browser simulator has the calculator's keypad
entries.body: it was a flat 5-column grid that followed no physical keyboard - DEL next to 9, ALPHA where x² is, arrows spread over two rows. It is now the fx-CG 50 layout: six function keys with the case's own captions, the SHIFT/OPTN/VARS/MENU and ALPHA blocks, the four-way pad on the right where the real one sits, and 7-8-9-DEL-AC / 4-5-6-×-÷ / 1-2-3-+-(−) / 0-.-×10ˣ-(−)-EXE. Keys Bench does not read are drawn as muted hardware rather than pretending to work; every live key is a real button with an aria-label. Checked at 320, 390 and 1280px: no horizontal scroll, smallest key 26px.

entries.title: The diagnostic add-in is on the site and in `dist/`
entries.body: `Bench-spike-0.0.2.g3a` is now published beside Bench's own `.g3a` - in `dist/` with a `SPIKE.txt` manifest, and on the downloads page under "The diagnostic add-in" - instead of being reachable only as a CI artifact on blob storage. The patch (`spike.diff`) is downloadable from the same place, so the spike can be had even when no binary has been built. It is still labelled as a diagnostic everywhere and still never appears on a release or next to the install button.

entries.title: The hero band stops cutting the `g`
entries.body: the yellow behind "in one" was clipping the descender of the `g` in "eighteen". Two causes: Tailwind's `text-5xl`/`text-6xl` set their own line-height and were beating the `h1`'s `leading-[1.35]`, so the heading ran on a 1.0 line box; and the band was an inline box, which paints over the font's content area, which at 60px is taller than the line. The heading now sets its line-height at every breakpoint and the band is an inline-block at line-height 1. `site/scripts/check-band.mjs` counts the neighbour pixels the band covers - 331 at 1280px before, 0 at every width from 320 to 1440px now - and runs in CI after the width sweep.

entries.title: A hardware report you can fill in on the calculator (V2, workstream J)
entries.body: Settings gained **F3**, which opens a screen listing the eight assumptions Bench makes about the CASIO filesystem, the font, ALPHA, the clock and the frame time. Each row starts at `not tried`; LEFT/RIGHT marks it `works` or `fails` after the matching test in `docs/HARDWARE.md`. F2 writes `state/hwreport.txt` in plain text, so the result comes off the calculator by copy rather than by retyping, and nothing is written at any other moment. The formatter is `src/core/hwreport.c` (63 native checks, including a buffer that is one byte too small), and `docs/HARDWARE.md` says how the file slots into the report.

entries.title: A shared number field and a history of answers (V2, workstream A5)
entries.body: `src/core/numedit.c` is the one place that decides what a numeric field accepts - digits, at most one dot, a lone zero replaced rather than stacked, a leading dot turned into `0.` - with `numedit_valid()` for "would numparse read this?" (54 checks). The moles screen was carrying its own copy, which is how `1.2.3` got in; it now uses the shared one. `src/core/history.c` keeps the last eight formatted results (33 checks) and the Root finder pushes every solve onto it, with F4 to show the list - a panel, not a file, so nothing is written to flash.

entries.title: The simulator runs in the browser (V2, workstream G)
entries.body: `tools/wasm/build.sh` compiles the add-in and `tools/sim/sim.c` - the same sources the screenshots come from - to a 300 KiB WebAssembly module. No emscripten and no Asyncify: zig carries clang, wasm-ld and wasi-libc, so the toolchain is one `pip install ziglang`. Blocking `getkey()` is fine because the module runs in a Web Worker, and keys and frames cross to the page through a SharedArrayBuffer (the deployment sends the two headers that allows). The page is `site/src/components/WasmSim.jsx`, the other half is `tools/wasm/worker.js`, and `tools/wasm/smoke.mjs` runs the module in Node - real keys in, real frames out as PPM - so the build is checked without a browser. The binary is committed (`site/public/sim/bench.wasm`) because Vercel has no C compiler; CI rebuilds it and fails if the committed copy is stale.

entries.title: Browser widths in CI (V2, workstream B)
entries.body: `site/scripts/check-widths.mjs` loads all eight routes at 320, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 px and fails on a horizontal scrollbar, an element that crosses the right edge or one wider than the viewport. Chromium could not be downloaded here, so the sweep has only run in CI; the result of that first run is in the pull request.

entries.title: Demo content (V2, workstream D)
entries.body: `demo/` holds three notes, three decks and a fortnight study log so a fresh install is not three empty screens. The text is written from scratch, not copied from a booklet or a past paper, and `demo/README.md` says in its first section that it needs human proofreading. `tests/test_demo_files.c` reads every demo file with the add-in's own parsers (108 checks) and fails on a single skipped line, so the sample cannot rot into something the calculator refuses to read.

entries.title: The site is eight pages, not one (V2)
entries.body: `/features`, `/simulator`, `/tutorial`, `/install`, `/downloads`, `/changelog` and `/about` join the landing page, which keeps its layout. `src/router.jsx` is a 120-line path switch with real `<a href>`s, so back, forward, middle-click and a shared link all work; `vercel.json` rewrites every path to `index.html`. Every route sets its own title, description, canonical and Open Graph image. `scripts/gen-stats.mjs` and `scripts/gen-changelog.mjs` write the numbers and the changelog from `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/tools.json` and `src/`, and `scripts/check-pages.mjs` renders all eight routes in Node and fails the build if one throws. Eight 1200x630 Open Graph cards come from `tools/brand/make_brand.py`. The canonical URL is now `bench-gdc.vercel.app` everywhere; `sitemap.xml` lists all eight routes.

entries.title: The simulator page is honest about the simulator
entries.body: the interactive WebAssembly build (workstream G) is not done, and the page says so instead of pretending. What it shows today is the real frame buffer: 75 captures made by the add-in's own simulator.

entries.title: Settings, five rows (V2)
entries.body: `src/core/settings.c` gains two keys, `angle_unit` (0 degrees, 1 radians) and `tour_done` (0 or 1). The screen now lists the unit the Triangle tool opens in and whether the first-run line on the home screen has been read; `app_triangle_init()` takes its starting unit from the setting, and F3/F4 still switch for that session only, without writing the file. A settings file from 1.0.0 still loads: the new keys fall back to their defaults. 687 native checks in `tests/test_settings.c`. Unverified on device.

entries.title: First-run hint (V2)
entries.body: with `tour_done 0` the home screen prints one line above the softkeys - "F1-F4 categories, F5 explains a tile, EXE opens it" - and opening help with F5 sets `tour_done` and writes the file once.

entries.title: Complex numbers (F6)
entries.body: `src/core/cplx.c` adds, subtracts, multiplies, divides (division by zero is a NaN, not a wrong number), raises to an integer power and reports the modulus, the argument (with `bm_atan2`, new in `src/core/mathfn.c`) and the polar form. `src/apps/app_cplx.c` shows all three at once, F2 cycles the operation, F3/F4 pick degrees or radians in the title bar. 37 native checks. Unverified on device.

entries.title: The M1 spike has its own artifact.
entries.body: It used to ride inside `bench-g3a`, next to the add-in, so the thing you download to get Bench offered two `.g3a` files and one of them printed diagnostics. `bench-g3a` now holds `Bench-<version>.g3a` and nothing else; the spike is in `bench-spike`. It was never a release asset and still is not.

entries.title: Root finder (F4)
entries.body: `src/core/roots.c` does bisection, Newton (numeric derivative, step 1e-6) and the secant method, keeping every iterate so the screen can show n, x, f(x) and the step size. `src/apps/app_roots.c` solves from the shared expression engine, F2 cycles the method, F3 solves, and a small plot marks each iterate on the curve. A bracket with no sign change, a zero slope and a parse error each get their own sentence and column. 40 native checks. Unverified on device.

entries.title: Statistics with working (F7)
entries.body: `src/core/stats.c` gives n, sum, mean, median, mode, range, both quartile methods, the outlier fences and the population and sample standard deviations (53 native checks). Paired data gets the least squares line, r and r squared. `src/apps/app_stats.c` adds values as you type them, shows the summary and a box plot, has a screen for the working and a screen for the regression. Unverified on device.

entries.title: SUVAT and projectiles (F10)
entries.body: `src/core/suvat.c` solves any three of s, u, v, a and t, one table entry per triple, and reports the equation each answer came from; when a quadratic gives two sensible times it keeps the first and names the second (73 native checks). `src/apps/app_suvat.c` fills the grid as you type, marks worked-out values with a dot, and draws the flight path for a launch speed, angle and height. Unverified on device.

entries.title: Moles and solutions (F11)
entries.body: `src/core/chem.c` covers n = m / Mr, c = n / V, pV = nRT with R in kPa dm3, dilution and the two percentages, refusing a zero where a formula divides (47 native checks). `src/apps/app_moles.c` has one mode per family, opens each on a worked example, and writes the substitution out under the answer. Unverified on device.

entries.title: Base and bits (F12)
entries.body: `src/core/base.c` parses and prints any base from 2 to 36, writes two's complement at 8, 16 and 32 bits (hex padded to the width, binary grouped in fours), and does AND, OR, XOR and logical shifts, refusing a shift of 63 or more (78 native checks). `src/apps/app_base.c` shows one value in five bases with all three widths, and a second tab for the operators; F2 opens the letter keyboard because the keypad has no A-F keys. Unverified on device.

entries.title: Lab graph (F8)
entries.body: `src/core/graph.c` fits a line to measured points and quotes the standard error of the gradient and the intercept from the residuals, plus a round axis range for the plot (42 native checks). `src/apps/app_graph.c` takes x, y and an error per point, lists them with the fit, and draws the graph with a bar through each point and the line of best fit. Unverified on device.

entries.title: Study log (F13)
entries.body: , **Notes v2 (F14)** and **Cards v2 (F15)**: a plain text log of what you studied and for how long, with totals, days logged and the longest streak (`src/core/logbook.c`, 56 native checks); the Notes footer now counts words as well as lines (`textsearch_words`, 6 more checks); and a Cards deck can be drilled in a mixed order inside each box (`leitner_shuffle`, deterministic for a session, 8 more checks). Bench cannot read the calendar - gint's date fields were never checked on the hardware - so a log entry takes the day after the newest one and UP/DOWN moves it. Unverified on device.

entries.title: Home tiles: the icon vanished on the selected tile.
entries.body: The icon was painted in the tool's accent colour on a tile filled with that same colour. Every foreground is now chosen by measurement (`col_better_on`), the icon is drawn with a 2 px outline, and a check samples the pixels afterwards. This is unverified on device: nobody has looked at the new screen on a calculator yet.

entries.title: Labels drawn in a colour too close to their background.
entries.body: Ink on red is 2.75:1, paper on teal 3.00:1, a red cursor on the yellow field 2.91:1. Text is now ink or blue on paper, and a selected tile is ink with paper text instead of a tinted tile with a paper plate under the label.

entries.title: The keyboard covered half of the note behind it.
entries.body: The modal now clears the content area first, and the space key is marked instead of being drawn as an empty cell.

entries.title: A 57-character file name ran across the whole title bar.
entries.body: `w_title()` now cuts the title to the room it has, and `STORE_NAME_MAX` went from 48 to 72 so such a file is listed at all.

entries.title: Markdown code spans painted over the character before them
entries.body: , and code was teal on shade (2.28:1). The background starts after the previous span, and code is ink on shade.

entries.title: The .g3a lives in the repository
entries.body: , at `dist/Bench-<version>.g3a`, with `BUILD.txt` recording the commit, size and SHA-256. Release assets and artifacts both come from blob storage, which some networks cannot reach; a git remote is plain git. CI refreshes `dist/` for tagged and automatic builds with a `[skip ci]` commit, so the copy does not go stale.

entries.title: The M1 spike as one patch
entries.body: `spike/spike.diff` holds the whole diagnostic add-in, generated from `spike/` by `tools/gen_spike_patch.py` (`make spike-patch`). `git apply spike/spike.diff` on a tree without `spike/` reproduces it byte for byte; CI fails if the patch and the sources disagree. The spike still is not on any release.

entries.title: Home screen v2
entries.body: four categories on F1..F4, a 3 x 2 page of tiles, page dots when a category has more than one page, and a dashboard strip on Study that counts the decks and notes on the card. The selected tile keeps the tool's accent as its fill, a 3 px border and a hard shadow; everything on it is coloured by measurement, and a subtitle the palette cannot carry gets a paper plate hugging the words. Unverified on device.

entries.title: Sequences and binomials (F5)
entries.body: `src/core/seq.c` does arithmetic and geometric terms and sums, the sum to infinity, exact `C(n,k)` (cancelling before multiplying, so it can answer up to n = 62 instead of wrapping) and Pascal's rows. `src/apps/app_seq.c` is three screens with the first few terms listed under the answers. 41 native checks. Unverified on device.

entries.title: Triangle solver (F2)
entries.body: `src/core/triangle.c` solves SSS, SAS, ASA/AAS and SSA from whatever is given, with the ambiguous SSA case reporting two triangles rather than silently picking one. `src/apps/app_triangle.c` is six fields, the answers written back into them, area and perimeter underneath, and F2 to swap between the two SSA triangles. 42 native checks. Unverified on device.

entries.title: Polynomials (F3)
entries.body: , quadratics and the arithmetic behind them: `src/core/poly.c` parses and prints polynomials, adds, subtracts, multiplies, expands `(ax + b)^n`, divides with quotient and remainder, solves a quadratic with real or complex roots, and factors over the rationals with the rational root theorem. `src/apps/app_poly.c` is three screens - quadratic (disc, roots, vertex, factor pair), expand, and roots from typed coefficients. 83 native checks. Unverified on device.

entries.title: Sig figs and standard form (F9)
entries.body: , the second of the fifteen: `src/core/sigfig.c` counts figures on the text (so `1200` is 2 and `1200.` is 4), rounds half-up on the decimal digits, and writes standard form and SI prefixes without a unit of its own. `src/apps/app_sigfig.c` has six modes - count, round to n figures, round to n decimals, standard form, SI prefix and a practice question with a score. 41 native checks. Unverified on device.

entries.title: Home screen: one clean block.
entries.body: A page shows only the rows it needs, the grid is centred in what is left, and the softkey strip reads Study, Math, Science, Tools, Help, About - F5 is help for the selected tile here as it is on every other screen, so Settings is a tile and not a second meaning for F5. Unverified on device.

entries.title: Function table (F1)
entries.body: , the first of the fifteen: `src/core/expr.c` is a shunting-yard parser (fixed 32-entry stack, implicit multiplication, column numbers on every error), `src/core/exprs.c` reads and writes the six slots, and `src/apps/app_function.c` is the slot list, the table and the probe. Unverified on device. degree conversion in plain C — no libm, no gint, so the calculator build and the host tests run the same code. 85 native checks against the textbook values. This is the ground the expression engine (A5) stands on. `lin_table.h` is generated by `tools/gen_lin_table.py`. 80 native checks. category, accent, icon, screen, help). The home screen reads it, and `tools/gen_tools_json.py` writes `docs/tools.json` from it via the host build. a dashboard strip on Study, and the selected tile's hard shadow. This is unverified on device.

entries.title: Help on every screen (F5).
entries.body: One page per tool, rendered from the tool's registry row: no second copy to drift. Paging (count, copy, clamp) is `src/core/help.c`, 37 native checks. On the home screen F5 shows the help for the tile under the cursor; in a tool it shows that tool's help; EXE or EXIT returns to the screen that asked. Unverified on device. empty divider cells, and an empty F5 slot advertises F5 as help. overlapping labels, labels off-screen, labels in the title bar or softkey strip, labels painted over, text under WCAG AA, softkey labels too wide, and icons that match their tile. 30 scripts, 0 findings. 89-character table cells. the checks that enforce them.

entries.title: Shell
entries.body: home screen with six tiles in the Bauhaus palette, title bar, softkey bar, lists, fields, modals, a progress bar and an on-screen keyboard. `src/platform/{screen,input,store,mem}` are the only files that call gint; `src/apps/app_menu.c` routes, `src/main.c` runs the loop.

entries.title: Pacer
entries.body: (`src/apps/app_pacer.c`): setup, plan with the checkpoint table, run with clock, marks, target, gap line and next checkpoint, done screen with the final gap.

entries.title: Uncertainty
entries.body: (`src/apps/app_uncert.c`): six operations, chain mode, value and absolute and percentage uncertainty on the result screen.

entries.title: Cards
entries.body: (`src/apps/app_cards.c`): deck list, deck report with problem lines, session with reveal, summary, box statistics; progress file written once at the end of a session.

entries.title: Notes
entries.body: (`src/apps/app_notes.c`): file list, Markdown and plain text rendering, scroll by line and page, search with wrap, heading list, per-line span drawing with the Phase A style (colour and underline).

entries.title: Number theory
entries.body: (`src/apps/app_numtheory.c`): nine functions, forms, results with steps for gcd and ext gcd, a progress bar for factorisation that EXIT cancels.

entries.title: Settings
entries.body: (`src/apps/app_settings.c`, `src/core/settings.c`): uncertainty figures, pacer checkpoint size, note width; the file is written only when a value changes.

entries.title: About
entries.body: (`src/apps/app_about.c`): version, build date, target, framebuffer and window sizes, largest free block, limits, and the Exam Mode note.

entries.title: Brand
entries.body: `assets-cg/icon-uns.png` and `icon-sel.png` (92x64, neobrutalist B with a red square and three bars), a wordmark SVG and a 1200x630 card, all drawn by `tools/brand/make_brand.py`. No bitmap fonts, no external assets.

entries.title: Host preview
entries.body: `tools/sim/` (a gint stand-in, key scripts and a tour) and `make sim`, `make shots`, which render every screen to `docs/images`.

entries.title: CI
entries.body: `.github/workflows/build.yml` runs the native tests, the Python tests, the preview, and builds `Bench-<version>.g3a` with the real fxSDK, attaching it to the release on a `v*` tag.

entries.title: Docs
entries.body: `README.md`, `docs/STATUS.md`, `docs/toolchain.md`, `docs/spike.md`, `site/` (the landing page: React 18 + Vite + Tailwind, deployed on Vercel).
